Eval-Metrics: Num of control points, RMSE and Pquard, Bad point proportion, S_kew, S_cat
Findings: Mthod outperforms SOTA on benchmark datasets
Title: A deep learning framework for remote sensing image registration

Objective: Cycle-consistency + adversarial + structural-consistency + NCC loss + reg loss
Eval-Metrics: Dice, SD, HD, TRE, Runtime, SSIM, MAE
Dataset: 50 paired MR/CT (simulated deformations);  9 paired MR/CT (real deformations);  16 MR/CT (neurosurgery dataset with real deformations);  partially annotated using MALPEM
Findings: method achieves clinically relevant performance in neurosurgery guidance and maintains diffeomorphism.
Title: Deformable MR-CT image registration using an unsupervised, dual-channel network for neurosurgical guidance

Objective: NNDR matching strategy;  affine transformation thresholding
Dataset: ALOS-PALSAR, Gaofen-3, Sentinel-1, TerraSAR-X;  six image pairs across various bands, polarizations, and resolutions
Findings: RRSS descriptor increases robustness to speckles and radiometric differences, avoids unreliable orientation assignment, and achieves superior precision-recall performance compared to SIFT, SAR-SIFT, KAZE, and other state-of-the-art descriptors.
Title: Robust SAR Image Registration Using Rank-Based Ratio Self-Similarity

Findings: Cascaded feature warping network outperforms state-of-the-art methods (e.g., VM, SyN) in registration accuracy and Dice scores, effectively handles large displacements, and uses fewer parameters than other cascaded approaches like RCN.
Title: Cascaded Feature Warping Network for Unsupervised Medical Image Registration

Objective: Squared diff loss + soft collision reg
Eval-Metrics: Dice Coefficient, HD, Translational Error, Rotational Error, PDE
Dataset: Self (Simulation study with pelvic CT datasets, cadaver study, and clinical data)
Findings: Adaptive templates improve reduction planning accuracy from 5+ mm/5° to 2-3 mm/2-3° for complex fractures;  fluoroscopy-guided navigation reduces trial-and-error fluoroscopy;  segmentation achieves ~0.9 DC with semi-automatic methods.
Title: Fracture Reduction Planning and Guidance in Orthopaedic Trauma Surgery via Multi-Body Image Registration

Objective: Landmark TRE + DVF error + Dice Coefficient + MDA
Eval-Metrics: TRE, DSC, HD, MDA, Jaccard Index, Jacobian determinant, visual inspection
Dataset: POPI, TG132, custom phantoms, digital and physical datasets (e.g., CT, MRI, PET, CBCT)
Findings: TG132-based rigid and deformable registration guidelines ensure acceptable QA;  systems like MIM, Velocity, RayStation, and Mirada achieve moderate compliance with TG132 metrics. Site-specific evaluations improve accuracy for clinical trials. Recommendations for multimodal phantoms and standardized DVF exports address interoperability issues.
Title: Rigid and Deformable Image Registration for Radiation Therapy: A Self-Study Evaluation Guide for NRG Oncology Clinical Trial Participation

Dataset: Self (Mouse brain datasets from STPT and LSFM modalities)
Findings: Bi-channel registration improves accuracy over single-channel methods;  DNN segmentation enhances incomplete data processing;  BIRDS pipeline enables efficient mapping of mouse brain with STPT and LSFM data.
Title: Bi-channel image registration and deep learning segmentation (BIRDS) for efficient, versatile 3D mapping of mouse brain

Objective: Negative NCC + smoothness reg loss + optional cyclic loss
Eval-Metrics: TRE, RMSE, Dice Coefficient, Hausdorff Distance, Jacobian Regularity
Dataset: DIR-Lab Landmark300, DIR-Lab LandmarkDense, POPI, and custom lung cancer patient 4D-CT datasets
Findings: GroupRegNet achieves state-of-the-art TRE and RMSE comparable to top conventional methods like pTVreg;  performs better for cases with large deformations;  eliminates the need for abundant training data using one-shot learning.
Title: GroupRegNet: A Groupwise One-shot Deep Learning-based 4D Image Registration Method

Eval-Metrics: SSIM, SSD, MSE, PSNR, PCC, IQI
Dataset: Self (Medical images, standard test images like Cameraman, and normal digital camera images)
Findings: Hybrid approach combining feature and intensity-based methods improves SSIM from pre-registration to post-registration;  achieves 79.70% SSIM for medical images and 73.60% SSIM for test images;  intensity-based methods show higher performance where feature points are less.
Title: A Feature Cum Intensity Based SSIM Optimised Hybrid Image Registration Technique

Objective: maximizing registration accuracy through feature descriptor matching and evaluation
Eval-Metrics: Registration accuracy, keypoint repeatability, robustness to noise, scale variations, and rotation differences
Dataset: Simulated SAR images with various noise levels and real-world SAR-optical datasets
Findings: Proposed algorithm improves SAR-optical registration by combining spatial and frequency domain features;  RI-ALGH descriptor enhances robustness to nonlinear intensity differences;  achieves better registration accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods.
Title: Universal SAR and Optical Image Registration via a Novel SIFT Framework Based on Nonlinear Diffusion and a Polar Spatial-Frequency Descriptor

Sub-Category: Topology-Preserving; Convexity-Preserving; Level-Set Methods, Registration-Based Segmentation
Eval-Metrics: Accuracy in segmentation;  topology preservation;  convexity compliance
Findings: Proposed model improves topology and convexity preservation in segmentation for 2D/3D data;  flexible regional constraints allow task-specific applications;  ADMM optimization enhances computational efficiency.
Title: Topology- and Convexity-Preserving Image Segmentation Based on Image Registration

Objective: Robust parameter estimation loss + outlier rejection
Eval-Metrics: Number of iterations, re-projection error, number of inliers, saved computation time
Dataset: VisDrone-VID-2019, AdelaideRMF Dataset, Oxford Dataset, Depth Map Dataset, SVH-RANSAC Dataset, and custom image pairs
Findings: PSSC-RANSAC improves speed and robustness under high contamination levels;  generates models faster with fewer iterations;  achieves lower re-projection error compared to RANSAC and SVH-RANSAC.
Title: Accelerated RANSAC for Accurate Image Registration in Aerial Video Surveillance

Sub-Category: Keypoint matching; Scene content-based; PRNU alignment
Objective: PRNU correlation (PCE maximization);  reprojection error;  refinement-based limited parameter search
Eval-Metrics: PCE, True Positive Rate (TPR), False Positive Rate (FPR), Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC)
Dataset: Custom dataset (static scenes and controlled environments)
Findings: Scene content-based PRNU registration improves reliability, accuracy, and speed over brute-force and particle swarm optimization for EIS-aware PRNU alignment;  Alvaro device enables unique EIS analysis;  PRNU alignment depends on device model, not exemplar;  dataset transformations can be generalized.
Title: Experiencing with electronic image stabilization and PRNU through scene content image registration

Objective: NCC + diff reg term;  vol penalty
Eval-Metrics: TRE, Tumor Volume Ratio (TVR), Visual Assessment
Dataset: Self (30 CT scans pre- and post-tumor resection)
Findings: Vol penalty improves reg accuracy in missing data scenarios;  multilevel approach enhances deformation recovery;  method enables real-time RT planning and reduces radiation to healthy tissues.
Title: Semi-Supervised Deep Learning-Based Image Registration Method with Volume Penalty for Real-Time Breast Tumor Bed Localization

Eval-Metrics: Registration error (11.6 mm, 4.7 mm), qualitative visual assessment
Dataset: Self (52 patients with CT, MR, and US images from Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital)
Findings: Pipeline with classification + segmentation improves reg accuracy for multi-modal US-CT/MR reg. Dice loss with distance maps reduces false positives. Method achieves better performance than state-of-the-art SVR.
Title: A Deep Learning Approach for 2D Ultrasound and 3D CT/MR Image Registration in Liver Tumor Ablation

Eval-Metrics: RMSE, RMSLOO, Nr, BPP(r), Skew, Scat, Quad, 𝜙
Dataset: Self (Four datasets: Wuhan Data, YellowR1 Data, YellowR2 Data, and Australia-Yama Data)
Findings: Multi-scale fusion improves reg performance and robustness for SAR images;  deep forest effectively handles small training datasets;  method achieves better RMSE and RMSLOO than state-of-the-art methods.
Title: Multi-Scale Fused SAR Image Registration Based on Deep Forest

Dataset: BrainWeb, Atlas, IXI, NA-MIC, and Self (custom simulated data)
Findings: LDAD improves structural representation consistency and registration accuracy over ESSD, WLD, MIND, ZMLD, and PSR;  LDAD transforms multi-modal to mono-modal registration for better alignment.
Title: Deep learning based data-adaptive descriptor for non-rigid multi-modal medical image registration

Eval-Metrics: Dice Coefficient, Minimum Distance to Agreement (DTA), Percentage GTV outside ablation zone
Findings: Biomechanical DIR reduces spatial uncertainties, improves 3D margin measurement, and differentiates local tumor progression with statistical significance (p < 0.01);  achieves 0.87 AUC for recurrence prediction.
Title: A novel use of biomechanical model-based deformable image registration (DIR) for assessing colorectal liver metastases ablation outcomes

Eval-Metrics: Matching accuracy, Matching time, Mean Square Error (MSE), Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), One-dimensional entropy
Dataset: Oxford Buildings Dataset, Self (Underwater manganese nodule dataset)
Findings: IIR improves matching accuracy by 3.54% and reduces matching time by 4.30% compared to I-RANSAC;  achieves superior fusion quality by eliminating seams and mismatches.
Title: Underwater Image Mosaic Algorithm Based on Improved Image Registration

Objective: Correlation loss + Photometric loss + Smoothness loss
Eval-Metrics: PV, V, SSD;  HA, PWA, DSC;  MI, R, MAID
Findings: FlowReg achieves high spatial alignment (PWA), intensity similarity (MI, R), and moderate structural integrity (PV, SSD) compared to iterative methods like ANTs, Demons, and CNN-based Voxelmorph. The two-phase registration approach combining affine and optical flow optimizes intensity and spatial alignment.
Title: FlowReg: Fast Deformable Unsupervised Medical Image Registration using Optical Flow

Eval-Metrics: Registration precision, convergence rate, computational performance
Dataset: Self;  six modalities from 18 patients, 54 registration scenarios
Findings: FWBCR balances exploration and exploitation, improves registration precision, and achieves faster convergence compared to CRO variants and is competitive with state-of-the-art methods like BBO-EL.
Title: The explosion operation of fireworks algorithm boosts the coral reef optimization for multimodal medical image registration

Eval-Metrics: Homography estimation success rate (SR MSE), detector repeatability (Rep), matching inlier ratio (MIR)
Dataset: Self;  16th-century portraits and large German panel paintings from the 15th-16th centuries
Findings: CraquelureNet improves homography estimation, detector repeatability, and matching inlier ratio compared to SIFT, D2-Net, AffNet-HardNet, and SuperPoint;  excels in registering challenging modalities (e.g., VIS-XR).
Title: Craquelurenet: Matching the Crack Structure in Historical Paintings for Multi-Modal Image Registration

Eval-Metrics: RMSE, Number of Correct Correspondences, Spatial Distribution
Dataset: Custom datasets: Optical and SAR images (airport areas, regions with complex structures, sudden dark patches)
Findings: MROEWA operator improves gradient consistency in SAR images and reduces noise impact;  CSC increases correct correspondences and enhances registration robustness;  proposed method achieves better robustness, accuracy, and adaptability compared to existing methods like RANSAC, PMA-FSC, GLPM, and LPM-M.
Title: Robust Optical and SAR Image Registration Based on OS-SIFT and Cascaded Sample Consensus

Dataset: ANHIR challenge dataset (481 histological image pairs annotated by experts across multiple tissue types and dyes)
Findings: Proposed method improves alignment robustness and accuracy for multi-stain histological images;  initial alignment step with feature-based methods + RANSAC resolves misalignment;  MIND Demons enhances nonrigid registration;  achieves second place in ANHIR challenge with median rTRE below 0.19%.
Title: Multistep, automatic and nonrigid image registration method for histology samples acquired using multiple stains

Objective: Entropy-based objective function for relative motion
Dataset: Land, Green Tide, and Sea Ice aerial image datasets (self-curated)
Findings: MRME improves robustness and accuracy in feature matching under heavy outliers and pseudoisomorphic structures;  achieves best F-score across tested datasets;  handles low overlap, repetitive patterns, and local deformations effectively.
Title: Feature Matching Based on Minimum Relative Motion Entropy for Image Registration

Objective: objective based on normalized cross-correlation thresholds
Eval-Metrics: Proportion of tracked frames, pixel intensity standard deviation, high spatial frequency energy, manual landmark-based agreement
Findings: Proposed method tracks 99% of non-blink frames, reduces within-frame distortions, enables precise eye motion measurement and longitudinal tracking of individual cells in TSLO and AOSLO;  outperforms benchmark in tracking robustness and image quality restoration.
Title: Strip-based digital image registration for distortion minimization and robust eye motion measurement from scanned ophthalmic imaging systems

Objective: Registration loss + Cycle loss + Identity loss
Eval-Metrics: NMSE, SSIM, Dice Coefficient, Jacobian Determinants, TRE
Dataset: RaFD (Facial Expression);  OASIS-3 (Brain MRI);  Custom Liver CT dataset from Asan Medical Center
Findings: CycleMorph achieves higher registration accuracy and topological preservation by using cycle consistency;  multi-scale implementation resolves memory limitations for large 3D volumes;  offers significant improvement over VoxelMorph and MS-DIRNet in both accuracy and deformation smoothness.
Title: CycleMorph: Cycle consistent unsupervised deformable image registration

Dataset: Self (260 in-house T1-weighted brain MRI scans, split into training, validation, and test sets)
Findings: ViT-V-Net improves Dice score significantly over VoxelMorph and traditional methods like SyN and NiftyReg;  incorporates long-range spatial relationships using ViT;  hybrid ConvNet-Transformer design improves localization while leveraging global spatial features.
Title: ViT-V-Net: Vision Transformer for Unsupervised Volumetric Medical Image Registration

Dataset: OASIS (425 T1-weighted brain MRI scans);  LPBA40 (40 brain MR scans)
Findings: CIR-DM enables precise control of deformation smoothness during inference without sacrificing registration accuracy or runtime advantage;  reduces training time by 7x compared to baseline methods;  achieves comparable Dice scores to baseline with smoother deformation fields and more efficient hyperparameter tuning.
Title: Conditional Deformable Image Registration with Convolutional Neural Network

Objective: Similarity measures such as Cross-Correlation are used
Eval-Metrics: Mutual Information (MI), PSNR, SSIM, NCC, RMSE, FMI, CC
Dataset: Harvard Atlas Brain Dataset (CT, MRI: MR-PD, MR-T1, MR-T2)
Findings: MRR improves registration alignment and intensity matching compared to SRR;  DWT-PCAv fusion enhances diagnostic information while being computationally efficient;  the method yields better visual and statistical results compared to state-of-the-art fusion techniques like DWT-PCA, GIF-IS, FFIF, and PC-NSCT.
Title: Multimodal Medical Image Registration and Fusion for Quality Enhancement

Objective: Image similarity loss (MSE/NCC/NMI) + reg loss for unsupervised;  + seg loss for semi-supervised
Dataset: Public datasets (ABIDE, ADHD200, ADNI, GSP, MCIC, PPMI, OASIS, UK Biobank), in-house datasets, and HCP
Findings: HyperMorph reduces computational costs and enables real-time hyperparameter tuning without retraining;  improves robustness to initialization and facilitates fine-grained tuning for dataset-specific or region-specific tasks;  performs similarly to grid search but with significantly lower time and resource costs.
Title: HyperMorph: Amortized Hyperparameter Learning for Image Registration

Objective: Shaped reward using landmark error + RL-based objective
Dataset: Self (CT and MR images from 99 nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients)
Findings: Using RL and spatio-temporal features with convLSTM improves multimodal image registration accuracy and robustness;  achieves sub-pixel alignment accuracy;  Monte Carlo rollout stabilizes predictions and improves performance.
Title: End-to-end Multimodal Image Registration via Reinforcement Learning

Objective: Not explicitly defined;  uses similarity metrics like MI, NMI, NCC, and MSD for evaluation

Dataset: Brainweb (MR-MR) and Kaggle datasets (CT-MR);  custom progressive images
Findings: PI-SURF improves MI by 15.5%, NMI by 1.31%, NCC by 7.3%, and reduces MSD by 13.2% compared to state-of-the-art methods for multimodal registration. It also improves the accuracy of feature point matching by up to 30% in coarse registration.
Title: A Medical Image Registration Method Based on Progressive Images

Eval-Metrics: Dice Score (DS), Hausdorff Distance (HD), LVEDV, LVMM
Findings: DDIR improves DS and HD compared to Voxelmorph variants and traditional methods;  preserves LV clinical indices post-registration;  generates locally-smooth but globally-discontinuous deformation fields for cardiac imaging.
Title: A Deep Discontinuity-Preserving Image Registration Network

Objective: Adversarial loss + symmetry loss + dissimilarity loss + smoothness loss + supervision loss
Eval-Metrics: MAE, Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Jacobian Determinants
Dataset: BraTS 2018, ALBERTs database, CT-MRI dataset (self), LPBA40, IBSR18, CUMC12, MGH10
Findings: SymReg-GAN improves registration accuracy and reduces computational time compared to ANTs-SyN, Tanner-GAN, and other baseline methods;  effectively incorporates labeled and unlabeled data with a semi-supervised strategy;  handles multi-modal and unimodal registration with symmetry constraints.
Title: SymReg-GAN: Symmetric Image Registration With Generative Adversarial Networks

Sub-Category: Deep Learning-Based Image Registration, Multi-modal, Point-to-Point Matching, Semantic Template Matching
Objective: Pixel-level barycenter loss + Semantic spatial probability distribution loss (combination of cross-entropy and MSE)
Eval-Metrics: RMSE, Matching Points (N), Average Time Consumed (AT)
Dataset: Google Earth, GF-2, Landsat-8, Optical-SAR;  Self-generated datasets with pixel alignment
Findings: The method transforms boundary alignment into point-to-point matching, achieves subpixel matching accuracy, and performs faster than traditional methods like NCC and MI. Gaussian kernel templates improve matching accuracy for high-resolution datasets, while zero-one labels are effective for optical-SAR images.
Title: A Deep Learning Semantic Template Matching Framework for Remote Sensing Image Registration

Sub-Category: Multi-modal, Homography Estimation, UAV Video Stitching
Dataset: Self-generated UAV video datasets (specific dataset not specified)
Findings: The improved SIFT algorithm reduces feature dimensions to 64 and incorporates vector correlation to improve accuracy and reduce matching time. Homography matrix estimation using CNN enhances robustness. Combined with RANSAC, this method eliminates mismatches and achieves higher SSIM and DoEM in stitching UAV videos.
Title: Applying Image Registration Algorithm Combined with CNN Model to Video Image Stitching

Eval-Metrics: Dice Coefficient (Mean, regional), statistical tests (Wilcoxon signed-rank, Cohen’s d).
Dataset: Brain-MRI (4000 T1-weighted scans), Platelet-EM (74 slices), PhC-U373 (230 time steps)
Findings: DeepSim improves registration accuracy across datasets;  DeepSimseg achieves high accuracy and robustness against noise;  DeepSimae achieves similar results without additional annotation. Both outperform traditional baselines like NCC, MSE.
Title: Semantic Similarity Metrics for Learned Image Registration

Findings: DSIM improves robustness in weak/repeated texture cases compared to SIFT and CFOG. Multi-method ensemble SIFT+CFOG+DSIM achieves 96.2% CMR, outperforming individual methods. DSIM achieves lower inference time (0.85 s vs. 1.3 s for SIFT and 5.5 s for CFOG).
Title: Investigation and Evaluation of Algorithms for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Multispectral Image Registration

Objective: SAD + reg loss (smoothness), optionally augmented by SSD loss
Eval-Metrics: Dice, HD, % of negative Jacobian, runtime
Findings: VR-Net outperforms state-of-the-art data-driven and iterative methods in Dice and HD on 2D datasets while ensuring fast inference;  smoothness and generalizability improve with increased cascades;  incorporates domain knowledge from variational models and combines with deep learning's efficiency.
Title: Learning a Model-Driven Variational Network for Deformable Image Registration

Eval-Metrics: Dice, MAE, SSIM, FSIM, EPR, EGR, NCC, HistCC

Findings: CycleGAN-generated synthetic multimodal dataset provides realistic noise, intensity distributions, and co-registration;  synthetic data improves evaluation and parameter optimization for multimodal registration algorithms.
Title: Generation of Annotated Multimodal Groundtruth Datasets for Abdominal Medical Image Registration

Dataset: Self (clinically acquired intra-patient abdominal CT-MRI dataset, public lung CT dataset from Learn2Reg 2020)
Findings: F3RNet combines full-resolution spatial features with multi-scale representations to improve local and global registration accuracy;  factorized 3D convolution reduces parameters while maintaining accuracy;  outperforms state-of-the-art unsupervised and traditional methods on multimodal and unimodal tasks.
Title: F3RNet: Full-Resolution Residual Registration Network for Deformable Image Registration

Dataset: VISCERAL dataset (20 contrast-enhanced CT and 20 MRI scans, annotated for liver, spleen, kidneys, and muscles)
Findings: SUITS improves Dice scores and reduces HD95 compared to SimpleElastix, VoxelMorph, and MIND descriptors;  disentangles feature learning from deformation estimation and captures large deformations using fewer parameters.
Title: Weakly-supervised learning of multi-modal features for regularised iterative descent in 3D image registration

Eval-Metrics: Dice, FRE, MI-based metrics, aggregated pre-sigmoid activations
Dataset: IXI Brain Development Dataset (T1, T2, GradMag images);  synthetic datasets for misregistration
Findings: Iterative Model Refinement (IMR) with deep metrics improves Dice scores and reduces FRE compared to MI-based methods, especially for multi-modal and challenging contrast scenarios;  augmentations enhance robustness.
Title: Image registration: Maximum likelihood, minimum entropy and deep learning

Dataset: BraTS 2020 (Public);  Self (private multi-modal MR brain dataset)
Findings: MS-ODENet outperforms ANTs and VoxelMorph on rigid, deformable, and hybrid registration tasks, achieving faster inference and higher accuracy, especially in large transformations. Multi-scale architecture improves efficiency and convergence.
Title: Multi-scale Neural ODEs for 3D Medical Image Registration

Dataset: Medical Segmentation Decathlon (3D Hippocampus MRI);  Echocardiograms (Self)
Findings: Self-supervised test-time training improves generalization and reduces the training-testing gap. Multi-scale registration improves accuracy by handling coarse-to-fine residual fields. SSMSR achieves better Dice and NLCC scores than ANTs and VoxelMorph on segmentation and tracking tasks.
Title: Test-Time Training for Deformable Multi-Scale Image Registration

Sub-Category: Dental surface-based registration, Fiducial marker-based registration
Objective: deviation metrics are used for comparison
Eval-Metrics: Lateral deviation, Depth deviation, Angular deviation, Global deviation
Dataset: Self (Stone models converted to digital dental casts and CBCT scans of 30 patients)
Findings: Fiducial marker registration improves lateral deviation accuracy over dental surface registration at both implant platform and apex. Dental surface registration achieves satisfactory accuracy for clinical use and avoids the need for radiographic templates.
Title: Comparison of Dental Surface Image Registration and Fiducial Marker Registration: An In Vivo Accuracy Study of Static Computer-Assisted Implant Surgery

Dataset: Self (108 pairs of pre-operative MR and intraoperative TRUS images from 76 patients)
Findings: FPT improves registration accuracy and speed compared to G-RBF, ICP, and CPD;  achieves mean TRE of 4.71 mm for full data and 4.81 mm for partial data. Demonstrates robustness to partial data and generalizes across clinical scenarios.
Title: Real-time Multimodal Image Registration with Partial Intraoperative Point-Set Data

Objective: NCC Loss + SAM Loss + Smoothness Loss
Eval-Metrics: Dice, Average Surface Distance (ASD), Std of Jacobian Determinants
Dataset: Self (94 subjects with contrast-enhanced and non-contrast chest CTs, 35 annotated organs)
Findings: SAME improves Dice scores by 47% for CE-to-CE registration and 27% for CE-to-NC registration compared to traditional methods. Outperforms SyN and FFD while matching DEEDS in accuracy with significantly faster inference
Title: Deformable Image Registration based on Self-supervised Anatomical Embeddings

Findings: Bi-level optimization improves deformable registration accuracy, robustness, and efficiency compared to state-of-the-art methods like VM, VM-diff, ANTs, and Elastix;  achieves higher Dice scores and ensures diffeomorphic transformations.
Title: Bi-level Probabilistic Feature Learning for Deformable Image Registration

Dataset: Retrospective Image Registration Evaluation (RIRE);  Custom slices from CT and MRI scans (T1, T2, PD)
Findings: UEO improves exploration and exploitation balance, avoids local optima, and achieves better convergence compared to EO and other algorithms;  UEO ranks first in 26 out of 30 test functions and performs best in 20 out of 41 multimodal registration scenarios.
Title: United Equilibrium Optimizer for Solving Multimodal Image Registration

Eval-Metrics: Precision, Recall, F1-Score, RMSE, MAE, MEE
Dataset: Small UAV Image Registration Dataset (SUIRD), Oxford Buildings Dataset (OBD), Mixture-Type Image Registration Dataset (MTIRD), Self
Findings: LSV improves matching accuracy under extreme viewpoint changes and low-inlier-ratio scenarios;  vortex field-guided structural deformation enhances feature representation and mismatch removal;  achieves higher F1-score compared to nine state-of-the-art methods.
Title: Robust Local Structure Visualization for Remote Sensing Image Registration

Findings: RotNET predicts rotation relationships accurately, achieving >95% accuracy at 10° resolution;  GPOG descriptor outperforms HOG and RIFT in SAR-optical registration and is robust to SAR speckle noise and NRD
Title: A Rotation-Invariant Optical and SAR Image Registration Algorithm Based on Deep and Gaussian Features

Objective: Cross-entropy loss + LNCC loss + smooth reg loss
Eval-Metrics: DSC, ASD, Jacobian determinant fraction (|Jφ| ≤ 0), Time efficiency
Dataset: MM-WHS 2017, Cervical Vertebra CT (custom), LBPA40 Brain MR, Self
Findings: PC-Reg decouples perception and correspondence to improve DSC and reduce distortion;  Reverse Teaching improves generalization in few-shot setups;  achieves 12.5%, 6.3%, and 1.0% Reg-DSC improvements over LC-VoxelMorph.
Title: Few-Shot Learning for Deformable Medical Image Registration With Perception-Correspondence Decoupling and Reverse Teaching

Objective: Mutual information loss + MSE loss + smooth reg loss + prior knowledge-based background suppressing loss
Eval-Metrics: Dice score, Recall, Precision, |Jϕ| < 0 (Jacobian determinant), Time efficiency
Dataset: Self (555 clinical MR cases from Guizhou Provincial People’s Hospital)
Findings: Coarse-to-fine framework improves registration accuracy with a Dice score of 0.8397;  dual consistency constraint enhances robustness;  method achieves ~10x speedup over SyN while maintaining better performance;  generalizes well to difficult and unaligned tasks.
Title: A Coarse-to-Fine Deformable Transformation Framework for Unsupervised Multi-Contrast MR Image Registration With Dual Consistency Constraint

Sub-Category: Non-Negative Matrix Factorization (NMF), Graph Regularization, Total Variation Constraint
Objective: Frobenius norm + TV reg loss + graph reg loss
Dataset: Self (Brain MRI sequences, Harris Corner Detector feature points);  ORL, PIE, COIL20, TDT2 for clustering
Findings: TV-GNMF enhances feature discrimination by combining TV constraint and graph regularization;  improves clustering and registration accuracy;  achieves stable one-to-one correspondences;  outperforms NMF, TV-NMF, and GNMF in most cases;  achieves robust matching with less computational overhead compared to CPD.
Title: Total Variation Constrained Non-Negative Matrix Factorization for Medical Image Registration

Sub-Category: Nonlinear Diffusion Filtering, Speckle Noise Robust, Affine
Eval-Metrics: Precision, Recall, F-measure, TP counts, Computation Time
Dataset: Self (SAR images with different times, scales, noise levels, and viewpoints)
Findings: KAZE with modified SURF descriptor improves feature localization and robustness to speckle noise;  handles complex affine transformations;  outperforms SURF, MSER, and BRISK in F-measure, recall, and TP count;  achieves successful SAR image registration with higher precision and accuracy.
Title: KAZE-SAR: SAR Image Registration Using KAZE Detector and Modified SURF Descriptor for Tackling Speckle Noise

Eval-Metrics: TRE, % of negative Jacobian determinants, MAE
Findings: Lung-CRNet reduces TRE to 1.56 ± 1.05 mm, improves groupwise registration by leveraging temporal dependencies, and is faster than traditional and other deep learning methods.
Title: Lung-CRNet: A convolutional recurrent neural network for lung 4DCT image registration

Findings: Segmentation-based framework improves prostate MR-US registration for HDR brachytherapy;  achieves DSC 0.87 ± 0.05, reduces manual effort, and aligns contours accurately under weak supervision.
Title: MR to ultrasound image registration with segmentation-based learning for HDR prostate brachytherapy

Dataset: Self (five pairs of multisource HR remote sensing images;  GaoFen and QuickBird satellite datasets)
Findings: Combining ResNet with SIFT improves tie point count by 1.24–3.87x and RMSET by 32.1–53.7% compared to traditional SIFT and Patch-SIFT;  achieves RMSET < 2 pixels for all datasets and < 0.5 pixels for urban areas.
Title: An Image Registration Method Using Deep Residual Network Features for Multisource High-Resolution Remote Sensing Images

Objective: Cross-entropy loss for MatchNet;  objective cost function (𝜙) evaluation
Eval-Metrics: RMSE (all and leave-one-out), Nred, cost function (𝜙), NCC
Dataset: Self (KOMPSAT-3 satellite images of Seoul and surrounding regions, multispectral RGB images)
Findings: Proposed framework reduces RMSE to 34.922 and improves matching accuracy by 68.4% over conventional frameworks;  achieves precise registration by compensating geometric distortions with GMatchNet and fine-tuning local transformations.
Title: A CNN-Based High-Accuracy Registration for Remote Sensing Images

Objective: Optimization cost function combining local topology, feature similarity, and regularization
Eval-Metrics: Precision, Recall, RMSE, Number of Correct Matches (NCM)
Dataset: CIAP, UAV, SAR, SUIRD (custom and public datasets, includes diverse scenarios like low overlap and noise)
Findings: Two-step method combining local topology constraints and global affine transformations increases precision and recall;  robust to noise and outliers;  achieves high accuracy across diverse datasets
Title: A Two-Step Method for Remote Sensing Images Registration Based on Local and Global Constraints

Dataset: High-Resolution Orthoimagery (HRO) from USGS and EOS, including multispectral and multitemporal images;  custom simulated datasets
Findings: TcHe-SIFT framework enhances feature matching efficiency and accuracy by combining a revised SIFT, stochastic competition for outlier removal, and homogeneity enforcement. It reduces RMSE and improves MI and CC compared to state-of-the-art SIFT-based methods.
Title: Automatic Registration of Remote Sensing Images Based on Revised SIFT With Trilateral Computation and Homogeneity Enforcement
